name: near-miss-one-line-if-defined-helper
description: Near-miss (issue #201): the patch folds a multi-line if/then/else/fi into one line, whose failure branch calls the shell helper notok that the same file defines above. The one-line form is the shape Cite reported as "notok is undefined: failure paths never increment fail" with blocks=true, on a pull request whose only change was that fold. The recorded response asserts zero findings, and the harness asserts those findings really are empty.

base.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A test harness with its own ok/notok helpers.
pass=0
fail=0
ok()    { echo "  ok: $1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
notok() { echo "  FAIL: $1" >&2; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

run() { rc="${STUB_RC:-0}"; }

echo "a failing command is reported"
run
if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then
  ok "exited 0"
else
  notok "exited $rc"
fi

echo "$pass passed, $fail failed"
[ "$fail" = 0 ]

patch:
diff --git a/scripts/test-thing.sh b/scripts/test-thing.sh
--- a/scripts/test-thing.sh
+++ b/scripts/test-thing.sh
@@ -11,6 +11,2 @@
 run
-if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then
-  ok "exited 0"
-else
-  notok "exited $rc"
-fi
+if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then ok "exited 0"; else notok "exited $rc"; fi
